newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communists won't back Russia spending cuts.
newsitem.headline: Communists won't back Russia spending cuts.

text.p: Communist Party chairman Gennady Zyuganov said on Tuesday his party would not support attempts to cut budget spending to cope with low tax revenues and said government policy would bankrupt Russia.

Zyuganov said the communists would "under no circumstances" back the sequestration of budget funds -- spending cuts which ministers say are needed to offset lower than expected tax revenues so far this year.

"Instead of revitalising industry and conducting a normal tax policy, ministers are keeping the old fiscal policy started by (former reform chief Yegor) Gaidar and here they will go bankrupt and break their necks," he told Reuters.
Parliamentary speaker Gennady Seleznyov, also a communist, said any attempt to sequester spending would be unpopular with the State Duma lower house, where communists are the largest faction.

The 1997 budget, approved after prolonged horse-trading and much debate, says the government must ask parliament to approve lower spending proposals if revenues are more than 10 percent below planned levels.

Ministers say plans on sequestration could be presented this month and the head of the Duma's tax committee said even so-called "protected items" could be at risk. These include payments for health, education and the military.
Zyuganov said this should not be allowed to happen.

"The protected items of the budget are called protected because they cannot be touched, especially by crooks like the ones gathered around Chubais today," he said, referring to reformist First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais.
